title: The prayer of the sick
intro: Illness does not cut us off from Allah – a sick person prays in the way they are able.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah does not burden anyone with more than they can bear. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:286)</small>

Illness is a test in the life of a believer. But even when we are ill, we must keep our connection with our Lord through Salah. Sometimes illness stops us from praying in the usual way, so Allah has made it easier for the sick.

learn.title: Can’t stand? → Sitting
learn.html: If a sick person cannot pray standing, they pray sitting, making ruku‘ and sajdah by bowing the head – bending lower for the sajdah than for the ruku‘.

learn.title: Can’t sit? → Lying down
learn.html: If they cannot even sit, they pray lying on their back, with their feet towards the Qiblah and their knees bent. Their head is raised a little so they can show the parts of the prayer by moving it. If they cannot move even these parts of the body, they may pray in their mind.

learn.title: Too ill to pray at all
learn.html: If the illness is so serious that the person cannot pray even in these easier ways, the prayer is delayed until they are able to pray. If this state lasts longer than one day, they do not have to make up the missed prayers.

learn.title: Unconscious or in a coma
learn.html: A sick person who is in a coma or unconscious for more than a day and a night – that is, if six or more prayers are missed – does not have to make up the prayers missed in that state.
The sick person judges their own state and prays in the best way their health allows.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “No hardship, sadness or illness – not even a worry – comes to a believer without Allah forgiving some of his sins because of it.” (Tirmidhi)

practice.title: The easier ways, step by step
practice.prompt: Put them in order, from the usual way to the easiest.
items: Sitting, bowing the head for ruku‘ and sajdah
Lying down, feet towards the Qiblah

practice.title: How will they pray?
practice.prompt: Choose the way each person will pray.

items.text: Has strong pains in the legs and can’t stand
Broke a leg but can sit up in a chair
Just had an operation and must not get out of bed
Is too weak even to sit up

questions.q: How does a sick person pray if they can’t stand?
options: Sitting, bowing the head for ruku‘ and sajdah
Standing anyway, even if it harms them

questions.q: When praying sitting, the head bends lower for …
options: the sajdah than for the ruku‘
the ruku‘ than for the sajdah

questions.q: Lying down, where do the feet point?
Someone was unconscious and missed six or more prayers. Must they make them up?
Who judges how the sick person can pray?

practice.title: Questions and task
prompts: 💬 How does a sick person pray? What about someone who is in a coma or unconscious?

📋 With your muallim, decide whether each person will pray, and how: a person with strong pains in the legs; a person who has just had an operation and must not get out of bed; a person who had an accident and cannot move their body; a person who has fainted; a person who is asleep; a person who cannot turn towards the Qiblah.
